description: Low-code editor for wiring together devices, APIs and services.

image_pins.reason: The Runtipi definition pins 5.0.6. Node-RED released 5.0.7 on 2026-09-08, a week later, and its changes include migrating to a patched JSONata and updating body-parser — dependency fixes worth having in an app whose whole purpose is evaluating expressions a person writes. Same repository, same minor line, one patch forward; the audit below covers 5.0.7 because that is what runs.

promotion.reason: Qualification is complete and the owner approved it on 2026-09-10. A real install proved the editor renders and holds its /comms websocket, that a deployed function node executes and returns its computed value, that the flow and its encrypted credentials survive a restart and a keep-data reinstall, that credentials are never written in plain text, that the container runs as UID 1000, and that delete-data removes everything owned. The reviewed pin moves 5.0.6 to 5.0.7 for the patched JSONata and body-parser. The judgement call is the editor's lack of a sign-in: it is bound to loopback only, asserted, and stated first in the risk notes, which is the same trust model as any local development tool. Proven on Windows with Docker's Linux engine only.

data_storage: Local Store managed folder / nodered, holding flows, credentials and installed nodes
risk_notes: Creates one Docker container and publishes one port on this computer's loopback interface only.
The editor has no sign-in. Anyone who can reach that address on this computer can open it, change flows and run them.

Flows execute code. A function node runs JavaScript and an exec node runs commands inside the container, with whatever network access the container has. That is what Node-RED is for, and it is worth knowing before you install it.

Keeps flows, credentials and any nodes you install in this app's managed folder. Credentials are encrypted with a key Node-RED writes into that same folder, so losing the folder loses the credentials with it.
The container writes as UID 1000 rather than as root.
Proven on Windows with Docker's Linux engine. macOS and Linux hosts are unverified.
